# Chris Pereira 彭家荣

> Chris Pereira (Chinese name 彭家荣, Peng Jiarong) is a British Canadian business leader, author and commentator with 20+ years in China. He is Founder and CEO of iMpact 美讯, founder of the Global Connect Show, and Founding Chairman of the Council for Global Brand Building (品信会, CGBB). He is a leading voice on Chinese companies going global (出海), brand trust and localization, and on what China reveals about the West.

## Key facts

- Former Senior Director of Global Public Affairs at Huawei.
- MBA, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST). Studied English Literature at York University (Toronto) and Chinese Language and Literature at Zhengzhou University.
- Teaches at Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University's International Business School.
- Forbes Top 30 Innovator (Forbes China, 2023). Judge, CES Innovation Awards (2026 and 2027).
- Author of Trust 《信任：中国企业全球化的黄金钥匙》 (Shenzhen Press Group, 2026, ISBN 9787550744516) and Rebuild 《新出海：中企海外本土化实战手册》 (China Renmin University Press, 2025, ISBN 9787300334882).
- Creator of the iMpact 5R Methodology: PR as the hub coordinating government relations (GR), business/industry leadership (BR), investor relations (IR), CSR/ESG and HR to build trusted local brands.
- Writes the weekly Substack 'Insights from China' and the Chinese-language WeChat account 美讯彭家荣. Op-eds in SCMP, Nikkei Asia, China Daily and Fortune China. Commentary on BBC, CGTN, CNBC, Bloomberg, Financial Times, Wall Street Journal, Reuters and more.
- Based in Shenzhen and Singapore. Speaks English and Mandarin. Available for keynotes, media commentary and corporate training (How to win with China, cross-cultural management, building trust in new markets).

## Core ideas

- Trust is the golden key for Chinese companies going global; product and price alone are not enough.
- Chinese companies should become trusted foreign brands, not pretend to be local: 'a German company from China' in Germany.
- CSR/ESG works as a 'good-guy card' (好人卡) that makes a foreign company stop being a stranger.
- Silence is the worst crisis strategy; engage media and local communities.
- The West can learn from China's openness and speed, and needs a renaissance of its own founding principles.
